doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

chapter: Growing up in Verona and Dry Jack
title: Cassette to Inner City Records deal
summary: Without a career plan the band sent a cassette to Inner City, was asked to record in New York, and visited Pat Metheny in Kansas City.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Did you have a clear idea, a goal, a concept of what it meant to make it in the music business?

No. No we didn’t even — we were just so into playing and you know getting gigs and playing out and developing the music. We didn’t think about that stuff. We knew that something was happening with the band that, wow we could, this could do something. So yeah I mean that’s sort of part of what you’re asking. But you know like the evolution of all of that was so organic you know. “Hey let’s make a cassette tape and send it to Inner City Records,” which is where we got the record. You know it was a cassette.
And you actually got a response?

They loved it. They said, “This is great, we’d like to explore this further. Can you do another recording” which we tried to do at this club in Kansas City. We sent that to him and he said, “Yeah this sounds good but it’s not quite the sound that we need for a recording.” I think there were some buzzes or whatever. And then about six months passed and then we got a call from them and they said, “We’d like you guys to come to New York City and record some records.”
Did you jump up and down at the time?

Oh man, you know it’s funny man we were in Kansas City gigging and had all the original material I had been writing, all of that had jelled. And so we were a force, we were so content and so happy to be putting this out. And I remember we got the record deal and we went to see Pat Metheny who we were friends with, and he just got his record deal with ECM with Lyle Mays and that band. So we thought oh man, this is cool you know.
